label: Third input token (t=2), stronger for r/t/y/g-like letters; weaker at t=3
explanation: A position detector early in the original phase. 83% of activation mass falls at t=2 (the third original token), where it fires on about half of all sequences, and 15% at t=3. It never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, or at t>=4 of the original phase, and only rarely during copy (1.8% of mass). Which token is input matters a lot: r (rate 0.21 over all steps), t, y and g are strongest, then s, j, e, u, m, d, x and 3. Top activations are r at t=2, e.g. z z [r]. Sequences starting with z/s/l and first occurrences of a token raise the rate somewhat. Position alone (t==2) gives F1 0.60 with mass recall 0.83; t in {2,3} gives recall 0.95 but precision 0.31. The token-gated predicate reaches dev F1 0.74 and mass recall 0.85. The token set is approximate, and the remaining errors are low-magnitude firings on other tokens at t=2/3.
